heroHeadline: Warsh Confirmed Fed Chair (May 13); April PPI +6.0% YoY — Hottest Since Dec 2022; Trump Arrives Beijing with CEOs; $30B Managed Trade Framework Set for Trump-Xi Summit May 14-15
heroSubtitle: May 13: A historic day of institutional and economic inflection. Kevin Warsh confirmed as Federal Reserve Chair by the Senate — Powell's era officially ends May 15; Warsh's first FOMC is June 9-10. April PPI +6.0% YoY (BLS, May 13) — the hottest producer prices since December 2022, with core +1.0% MoM (vs +0.4% estimate) — confirms full pipeline inflation is accelerating, arriving the day after April CPI 3.8% YoY (May 12). Two consecutive days of record inflation data entering the Warsh era. US 10Y yield rose to ~4.50-4.55%; CME hike odds ~30% by year-end. On diplomacy: Seoul Day 2 (Bessent-He) was 'candid, in-depth, constructive' (Xinhua) — a $30B-for-$30B reciprocal managed trade framework confirmed as the primary deliverable for the Trump-Xi Beijing summit (May 14-15), alongside a critical minerals/rare earths cooperation deal and Chinese purchase commitments. Trump arrived Beijing with a delegation of American CEOs. Iran cooperation on the Hormuz ceasefire remains the wildcard — if Xi delivers on pressuring Tehran, it could cut Brent from ~$105-110 to $80-90, reducing US CPI by ~0.5-0.8pp within 90 days. Recession probabilities: Goldman ~20%, JPMorgan ~25%, Moody's ~40%. Section 122 tariff cliff July 23 (71 days). The stagflation trap is deepest since the Iran war began — the Warsh Fed and Trump-Xi summit are the twin keys to its resolution.
